lines.name: Julie Whitfield
lines.say: Morning, love. Did you sleep alright? My knee's grumbling again, so I'll take it steady today. I'll get dressed and pop down and put the kettle on. Are you wanting toast or a proper breakfast? And remind me, did Jack say he'd be in for tea tonight? I want to know what to get in at the shops.
lines.do: Sits up slowly, rubs her knee, and reaches for her dressing gown and cardigan

lines.name: Andrew Whitfield
lines.say: Slept fine, thanks. Sorry about the knee, take it steady and I'll do the stairs runs today. Toast will do me, maybe an egg if there's one going. As for Jack, I think he said he'd be in, but I wouldn't swear to it. He mumbled something about the pub quiz, so I'll text him and find out.
lines.do: Pulls on trousers and a jumper, then picks up his phone from the bedside table.

lines.name: Julie Whitfield
lines.say: Oh, bless him, the pub quiz. Well, if he's out I'll just do a smaller tea, so do ask him, love. And an egg is no trouble, I think we've got half a dozen left. Right, I'm going down. Mind, you don't have to do all the stairs runs, I'll manage the odd one!
lines.do: Pulls on her cardigan, gets up slowly with a hand on the bedside, and heads for the door.

gists: Kitchen breakfast with the family. Mum's baking flapjacks and maybe cheese scones after lunch and I said I'd help if I'm up to it. Dad's out for a walk and the butcher's, and shepherd's pie is for tea. Jack has a kickabout at 11 and the pub at 4. We couldn't crack Dad's 7-letter crossword clue. Prowler probably isn't it because it's a homophone.

lines.name: Andrew Whitfield
lines.say: Jack's in for tea, love. He's got a kickabout at eleven and the pub at four with a mate, so not the quiz after all. I said I'd save him a plate.
lines.do: Fills the kettle again and drops bread in the toaster, then glances at the crossword.

lines.name: Julie Whitfield
lines.say: Oh good, a kickabout, that'll work off his breakfast. Mind you, will he actually have any breakfast first? He never does, bless him. I'll do a bit of shepherd's pie for tea then, he likes that. Do you want that egg boiled or fried, love?
lines.do: Fills a mug from the pot, then gets the egg box out of the fridge and checks it.

lines.name: Andrew Whitfield
lines.say: Fried, please, if it's no bother. Runny yolk, if you can manage it. Shepherd's pie sounds good. I'll nip out after my walk and see if the butcher's got any decent mince, save you the knee.
lines.do: Pours the tea, then sits down with the crossword and a pen.

lines.name: Sophie Whitfield
lines.do: comes in

lines.name: Julie Whitfield
lines.say: Morning, Sophie love! Kettle's just boiled, there's tea in the pot. How are you feeling today? Did you sleep alright? I'm doing Andrew a fried egg, do you want one too, or just toast? You need something in you.
lines.do: Cracks an egg into the pan and reaches for another mug for Sophie.

lines.name: Sophie Whitfield
lines.say: Morning. Slept alright, just a bit late off. I'm fine, honestly. Just toast for me, thanks, Mum. I'll pour my own tea.
lines.do: Pours a mug of tea from the pot and sits down at the table.

lines.name: Julie Whitfield
lines.say: Just toast, love? Go on then, but I'll put some butter on it and you have a banana with it, no arguments! Right, Andrew, there's your egg, nice and runny. Sophie, have you got anything on today, or are you having a quiet one? I'm doing a bit of baking later if you fancy helping, only if you feel up to it.
lines.do: Slides the fried egg onto a plate for Andrew, pops two slices of bread in the toaster for Sophie, and puts the banana bowl on the table.

lines.name: Sophie Whitfield
lines.say: Quiet one, I think. I might do the puzzle game later. Baking sounds nice though, maybe after lunch if I'm up to it. What are you making?
lines.do: Takes the banana and peels it, sipping tea.

lines.name: Julie Whitfield
lines.say: Oh, I thought I'd do a batch of flapjacks, love, and maybe a few cheese scones if there's enough cheese in the fridge. Shepherd's pie's for tea, so nothing too heavy. After lunch is perfect, no rush, only if you feel up to it. And Andrew, don't forget the mince, a pound will do, and ask if he's got any of that nice lean one.
lines.do: Plates up toast, spreads butter on it, and brings it over to Sophie with a smile.

lines.name: Sophie Whitfield
lines.say: Thanks, Mum. Flapjacks are a good shout. I'll have a go at the scones too if I'm up to it. Dad, how's the crossword going?
lines.do: Eats toast and banana, sips tea

lines.name: Julie Whitfield
lines.say: Go on, Andrew, how is it going? Only don't tell me if it's one of those cryptic ones, I'll be at it all morning! Sophie, finish that banana, love. Right, I'll just get the oven on for later and have a look at the cheese.
lines.do: Sips tea, then opens the fridge and checks the cheese.

lines.name: Sophie Whitfield
lines.say: Dad, you've gone quiet. Is it a stuck one? Read me a clue and I'll have a go while I finish this.
lines.do: Finishes the banana and picks up her tea.

lines.name: Andrew Whitfield
lines.say: Sorry, I was miles away. Not stuck so much as being stubborn. Seven letters, "Walks quietly round the edge of the park, we hear", and I've got the P and the R and nothing else. Have a go if you like. Then I'll finish this egg before it goes cold and head out for the walk.
lines.do: Looks up from the crossword, taps the pen on the page, then cuts into the egg.

lines.name: Sophie Whitfield
lines.say: Hmm. Walks quietly, so something sneaky. Prowler? That's seven, P and R at the start and the end. I can't make the "we hear" part work though, so it might just be me forcing it. Does it fit with anything else you've got?
lines.do: Leans over to look at the crossword, holding her mug.

lines.name: Andrew Whitfield
lines.say: Prowler's a decent shot, and it does fit the letters. But the "we hear" bit usually means a homophone, so I'd expect the answer to sound like something else. Park edge, walks quietly... I'll chew on it while I'm out. If it comes to me by the pond, I'll text you a smug message. Right, egg first.
lines.do: Eats the egg with toast, then finishes his tea.

lines.name: Jack Whitfield
lines.do: comes in

lines.name: Sophie Whitfield
lines.say: Morning, Jack. Kickabout at eleven, I hear. Dad's stuck on a crossword clue if you fancy a go. Oh, and can you leave the bathroom in a fit state today? Ta.
lines.do: Finishes tea and glances at Jack with a dry half-smile.

lines.name: Jack Whitfield
lines.say: Morning all. Ha, yeah yeah, bathroom's fine, to be fair I haven't even been in yet. Dad, what's the clue? Seven letters, P and R? Prowler's got to be close, honestly. Is that a homophone thing, like sounds like something else? Mum, is there any toast going, I'm starving.
lines.do: Pulls out a chair, nicks a banana from the bowl and peers at the crossword

lines.name: Julie Whitfield
lines.say: Morning, love! Toast coming up, sit yourself down. Two slices or three? And have that banana with it, not instead of it! Honestly, Jack, you'd go all morning on nothing if I let you. Is it going to be eggs too, or just toast? I've still got a couple going.
lines.do: Pops three slices of bread in the toaster and gets the butter out

lines.name: Jack Whitfield
lines.say: Three slices please mum, you're a legend. Just toast though, I'll have the banana with it, promise. Dad, "walks quietly round the edge of the park, we hear"... so it sounds like something else. Prowler, prowler... hang on, is it something like "pro-" and then a sound-alike? Honestly I'm rubbish at these, I'll just stare at it till it comes to me, ha.
lines.do: Peels the banana and sits at the table, leaning over the crossword

lines.name: Sophie Whitfield
lines.say: Prowler's probably wrong then. Sounds like something else... "prowler" doesn't really sound like anything. Hang on, park edge, walks quietly. Pad... no. I'll leave you to it, Dad. I'm going to take my tea through and do the puzzle game for a bit.
lines.do: Takes her mug and plate, heads off towards the living room.

lines.name: Julie Whitfield
lines.say: Here you go, Jack love, toast's up. Butter's on the table. Now, you're not to rush that banana. Andrew, what about "prowler" being a sound-alike of something? Oh, I'm no good at these, I'll leave it to you clever ones. Jack, are you in for tea tonight, or is it the quiz? I'm doing shepherd's pie.
lines.do: Pops the toast out, buttering it quickly, and slides the plate across to Jack.

lines.name: Jack Whitfield
lines.say: Tea's sorted mum, I told dad earlier, I'm in for it. Shepherd's pie, lovely. Dad, what about "pacer"? No wait, that's five. Hang on, "we hear"... "pro" and something... honestly I'm useless, mate, I'll leave it with you and the pond.
lines.do: Butters the toast and eats it, glancing at the clock

lines.name: Julie Whitfield
lines.say: Ooh, hang on, "prowler" and "we hear"... what about "progler"? No, that's nonsense, listen to me! Right, I'll leave it with you, Andrew. Don't forget that mince on your walk, love, a pound of the lean if he's got it. And Jack, finish that banana. Then I'll get these flapjacks started before I walk down to the shops myself.
lines.do: Gets the oats, butter and golden syrup out of the cupboard and starts weighing things out.

lines.name: Jack Whitfield
lines.say: Ha, "pro-wler"... hang on, what about "prowler" sounding like "prowl her"? Nah, that's rubbish. Right, I'll finish this and go sort my boots out. Dad, text me if you get it by the pond, I want to know now.
lines.do: Finishes the toast and banana, takes the plate to the side, glances at the clock

lines.name: Julie Whitfield
lines.say: Ooh, hang on, "prowler" and "prowl her"... Jack, you daft thing! Right, I'll leave you all to it. Jack, boots by the back door, not in the hall, please, love. And Andrew, don't forget your scarf, it's nippy out. Flapjacks first, then I'll see about the shops.
lines.do: Weighs oats, butter and golden syrup into a pan and puts it on a low heat, stirring.

lines.name: Jack Whitfield

lines.name: Jack Whitfield

lines.name: Andrew Whitfield
lines.say: Yes, the back one again. There's a clump of leaves at the corner that's been overflowing every time it rains. Tomorrow's fine, no rush. Shepherd's pie sounds right, I'll do the carrots. Go and kick something, and tell Dan he's a disgrace.

lines.name: Jack Whitfield
lines.say: Ha, will do, I'll tell him he's a disgrace. Right, I'll ring him and see where he's got to. See you at tea, dad, good luck with the clue.

lines.name: Andrew Whitfield

lines.name: Sophie Whitfield
lines.do: walks slowly along the path at the edge of the park, glancing over at Jack's kickabout

lines.name: Jack Whitfield
lines.say: Soph! Didn't think you'd make it out, nice one. Honestly it's well fresh today, isn't it? Dan's useless, he's ten minutes late to everything, but we've had a decent kickabout. You want to sit on the bench for a bit, or are you just doing a lap?
lines.do: jogs over to the path, a bit out of breath, ball under one arm

lines.name: Sophie Whitfield
lines.say: Yeah, bit of a bench would be good actually. I've done most of a lap already. Is Dan there yet or is it just you two knocking about?
lines.do: nods towards the bench and starts walking over to it

lines.name: Jack Whitfield
lines.say: Yeah Dan turned up in the end, mate, honestly about ten minutes late like I said. He's just nipped off to get a drink, he'll be back in a sec. We're only knocking about, nothing serious. How're you feeling, though? Is it alright out here or is it too cold for you? We can sit a while, I'm not fussed.
lines.do: walks over to the bench with Sophie and sits down, putting the ball by his feet

lines.name: Sophie Whitfield
lines.say: It's fine, a bit nippy but I've got my big coat on. I'll sit for ten minutes and then head back for lunch. Mum's got the flapjacks on, so I should probably show my face.
lines.do: sits down on the bench and pulls her coat tighter

lines.name: Jack Whitfield
lines.say: Flapjacks, nice. Save me one, mate, honestly I'll be back in a bit once Dan's finished his drink. Dad's still stuck on that crossword clue, you know. Did he text you the answer yet?
lines.do: leans back on the bench, rolling the ball under his foot

lines.name: Sophie Whitfield
lines.say: Not yet, no. He's still on that seven-letter one. I did suggest a couple, but apparently they're all wrong. I'll have a look when I'm back. Go on, Dan's probably waiting. I'll sit a few more minutes and then head back.
lines.do: watches the ball roll under his foot, tucks hands into coat pockets

lines.name: Jack Whitfield
lines.say: Go on then, I'll get back to it, Dan's probably wandering round with a Lucozade by now. Don't sit too long though, Soph, you'll freeze. Save me a flapjack, honestly, mum'll say they're gone and they won't be. See you in a bit, yeah?
lines.do: picks up the ball, stands, and jogs back toward the pitch

lines.name: Andrew Whitfield
lines.say: Mince is in the fridge bag, I'll sort it out for tonight after lunch. The back gutter's got a proper clump at the corner, but it's too damp to go up today, so I'll leave it till tomorrow when Jack can hold the ladder. How's Sophie doing today, has she eaten anything yet?
lines.do: Puts the butcher's bag in the fridge, washes hands, and sits down at the table.

lines.name: Sophie Whitfield
lines.do: comes in

lines.name: Julie Whitfield
lines.say: Hello love, there you are! Sit yourself down. I was just about to ask, have you had anything yet today? There's mince on for tonight, but for now I can do you a cheese sandwich or some soup, and there's scones after, they're still a bit warm. Andrew, tomorrow's fine for the gutters, just don't go up without Jack holding it, I mean it!
lines.do: Gets bowls out and pulls a chair out for Sophie

lines.name: Andrew Whitfield
lines.say: Soup sounds good to me too, Julie. Sophie, if you fancy it, I'll have the scone with you afterwards. They smell right from here. And no ladder today, I promise. I've been told twice already.
lines.do: Sits at the table and takes a bowl, glancing at Sophie to see how she's looking.

lines.name: Sophie Whitfield
lines.say: Soup's great, thanks Mum. I had a flapjack when I got in, so I'm not starving, but I'll have a bowl. Jack says to save him a scone, by the way. He's back for dinner.
lines.do: Sits down at the table and takes the bowl, unbuttoning her big coat.

lines.name: Julie Whitfield
lines.say: Right, soup coming up, it's only the tin one but it's the good tomato. Mind, it's hot, Sophie love, let it cool a minute. I'll save Jack a scone, bless him, two if he behaves! Is he eating properly at that kickabout, though, or just living on flapjacks? And how are you feeling today, love, any better than yesterday?
lines.do: Heats the soup, ladles it into the bowls and brings them to the table, then sits down

lines.name: Andrew Whitfield
lines.say: He's fine, Julie, he'll have had a banana and a sausage roll at some point. Sophie, careful with that soup, it really is hot. Did you get out at all this morning, or have you been resting? No pressure, I'm just asking.
lines.do: Blows on his own soup and breaks a bit of bread.

lines.name: Sophie Whitfield
lines.say: I got out for a bit, did a lap round the park and sat on the bench for a while. It was fine, just nippy. Then I came back for a flapjack. Yesterday was a bit worse, today's about average.
lines.do: Blows on the soup and takes a spoonful.

lines.name: Julie Whitfield
lines.say: Well, a lap round the park is good going, love, as long as you wrapped up. Keep that coat on if you're chilly, I don't mind a bit of soup on the cuff! Andrew, there's butter for the bread in the door of the fridge, and have a scone after, they're the cheese ones. Sophie, do you fancy a bit of a rest this afternoon, or have you got plans? I'm only going to put my knee up with the radio and a word search.
lines.do: Pushes the butter dish across the table and tucks into her own soup.

lines.name: Andrew Whitfield
lines.say: Good to hear. A lap of the park is plenty on a nippy day. I'll have the cheese scone in a minute, Julie, once this soup's gone down. Sophie, if you're resting this afternoon, I'll be in the living room with the paper and that crossword clue, so shout if you want anything.
lines.do: Tears off a piece of bread, butters it and keeps eating his soup.

lines.name: Sophie Whitfield
lines.say: I'll probably just rest and watch the football with Dad in a bit. Might have a scone first though. Mum, how's the knee today?
lines.do: Eats soup, tears a bit of bread.

lines.name: Julie Whitfield
lines.say: Oh, it's grumbling a bit, love, but nothing dreadful. It always plays up when it's damp, bless it. I'll get it up on the pouffe with the radio and it'll settle. Now, eat your soup before it goes cold, and have a scone after, they're nice with a bit of butter. Andrew, don't let her sit too near the radiator if she's got that big coat on, she'll get all flushed!
lines.do: Tears a bit of bread and carries on with her soup.

lines.name: Sophie Whitfield
lines.say: Scones sound good, Mum. Dad, I'll come through for the football in a bit. Is it the early kick-off today?
lines.do: Finishes the soup and reaches for a scone.

lines.name: Andrew Whitfield
lines.say: I think it's the three o'clock one, so you've got a few minutes yet. Finish your scone and come through whenever you like. I'll clear these bowls first, Julie, you stay put with that knee.
lines.do: Takes the cheese scone, stacks his empty bowl and reaches for Julie's.

lines.name: Julie Whitfield
lines.say: Thank you, love, you're a star. Mind, I'll bring the plates through, I'm not completely useless! Sophie, have another scone if you fancy, and I've put Jack's two by on the side, so nobody nick them! Right, radio and word search for me. Shout if you need anything, either of you.
lines.do: Gets up slowly, stacks the plates, wipes the table, then covers Jack's scones with a tea towel.

lines.name: Sophie Whitfield
lines.say: Cheers Mum. I'll take the scone through with me and get the football on with Dad.
lines.do: Takes a scone, gets up and heads for the living room.

lines.do: Walks into the kitchen, grabs cutlery from the drawer and starts laying the table

lines.name: Julie Whitfield
lines.say: Oh hello love, you're just in time! Sophie's coming down, I think, I'll give her a shout in a minute. Dad's got the mince, so ten minutes or so, isn't it, Andrew? Jack, mind the good forks, they're in the left-hand drawer. Have you eaten anything today, bless you? You've got that look.
lines.do: Stirs the veg pan, glances at the clock

lines.name: Sophie Whitfield
lines.say: Coming, mum. And yes, I've eaten, don't fuss. Toast, at some point.
lines.do: comes in

lines.name: Jack Whitfield
lines.say: Yeah, I had a bit of a sandwich earlier, mum, honestly, I'm fine. Toast doesn't count though, Soph, to be fair. Right, forks, left-hand drawer, got them. Dad, is that shepherd's pie with the cheese on top? Please say cheese.
lines.do: Keeps laying the table, putting out four sets of cutlery and the good forks

lines.name: Andrew Whitfield
lines.say: Cheese, yes, Jack, I'm not a monster. It's shepherd's pie, and it's got a bit of cheddar on top that I'll put under the grill for the last few minutes. Ten minutes or so, Julie's about right. Soph, toast does count as a food group in this house, but I'll make sure you get a decent portion of this as well.
lines.do: Spoons the mince into the pie dish, tops the mash and scatters grated cheese over it

lines.name: Julie Whitfield
lines.say: Lovely, that's everyone then. Soph, love, sit yourself down by the radiator, you'll be warmer there. Jack, can you grab the gravy jug from the top cupboard and the water jug while you're up? I'll do the veg in a minute, the carrots are nearly there. Andrew, don't forget the grill, last time it caught and we had smoke everywhere!
lines.do: Drains the carrots and checks the peas, then wipes her hands on the tea towel

lines.name: Sophie Whitfield
lines.say: Fine, I'm sitting. Want me to do the water jug, Jack? I'm closer to the tap anyway.
lines.do: sits by the radiator, then gets up again to fill the water jug

lines.name: Jack Whitfield
lines.say: Go on then, Soph, cheers. I'll get the gravy jug, top cupboard, yeah? Honestly, I always forget which one it is, it's the blue one, isn't it? Mum, do you want the veg dishes out as well?
lines.do: Finishes the last place setting, then reaches up into the top cupboard for the gravy jug

lines.name: Andrew Whitfield
lines.say: Jack, the gravy jug's the blue one, yes, though I'd check it's not the one with the chipped spout. Julie, the grill's on my list, I'm putting the pie under in a minute and I'll stand over it like a hawk. Veg dishes would be good, Jack, thanks.
lines.do: Slides the pie dish under the grill and sets a timer on the cooker.

lines.name: Julie Whitfield
lines.say: Lovely, thanks both. Right, peas are done, so I'll get the veg into the dishes. Sophie, love, mind that jug, it's heavy when it's full, don't strain yourself. Jack, pop the dishes on the table when I've done them, and the mats are in the second drawer, I don't want the table marked.
lines.do: Spoons carrots and peas into the veg dishes and wipes the edges with the tea towel

lines.name: Sophie Whitfield
lines.say: Jug's full. Mum, I've got it, it's not that heavy. Jack, can you grab the mats? I'll put it on the table.
lines.do: Fills the water jug and carries it to the table, sits back down by the radiator.

lines.name: Jack Whitfield
lines.say: Mats, yeah, second drawer, on it. Honestly I'd forget my own head. Veg dishes too, mum, pass them over when they're done. Cheers for the jug, Soph.
lines.do: Fetches the mats from the second drawer, puts them down and carries the veg dishes to the table

lines.name: Andrew Whitfield
lines.say: Right, that's about four minutes on the timer. Julie, I'm watching it, no smoke this time, I promise. Jack, is the blue jug the chipped one or not? Sophie, if you're sitting, you can pick the gravy. Granules or the proper stuff from the pan juices, I made a bit.
lines.do: Stands by the grill, glancing at the timer, and wipes the worktop

lines.name: Julie Whitfield
lines.say: Proper gravy from the pan juices, Andrew, ooh lovely, Soph can you stir it for him? And Jack, it's the blue one, love, but the spout's only got a tiny chip, it won't hurt. Right, I'll bring the veg over. Have we got the sauce out for your dad? It's in the fridge door.
lines.do: Carries the last of the veg dish to the table and fetches the sauce from the fridge door

lines.name: Sophie Whitfield
lines.say: Yeah, I'll stir it. Dad, is the pan juices thing already thickened or do you want me to put some flour in?
lines.do: Gets up from the radiator and goes over to the hob to stir the gravy.

lines.name: Andrew Whitfield
lines.say: Sophie, it's just the pan juices with a bit of cornflour in, so it's already near enough. Give it a stir and see. If it's too thin, a splash of the carrot water will do, but I'd leave it be. Jack, the blue jug's fine, a tiny chip never hurt anyone. Sauce on the table, lovely. Timer's nearly up, so everyone sit down and I'll bring this over.
lines.do: Keeps an eye on the timer, then takes the pie out from under the grill with oven gloves.

lines.name: Jack Whitfield
lines.say: Sitting, sitting. Honestly that looks unreal, dad. Soph, how's the gravy, is it thick enough or are we having soup? Mum, you sit down as well, I'll grab the sauce and plates if we need them.
lines.do: Pulls out a chair and sits at the table, pushing the sauce towards the middle

lines.name: Julie Whitfield
lines.say: Right, I'm sitting, I'm sitting! Ooh, that does look lovely, Andrew. Soph, is the gravy all right, love? Jack, plates are warming on the side there, would you mind? Then I'll get the serving spoon. Mind, it'll be hot, use the gloves!
lines.do: Puts the sauce down, sits at the table and rests her knee

lines.name: Sophie Whitfield
lines.say: Gravy's fine, dad, it's thick enough. Not soup. I'll bring it over.
lines.do: Stirs the gravy, pours it into the blue jug and carries it to the table, then sits down.

lines.name: Andrew Whitfield
lines.say: Right, mind yourselves, it's hot. Jack, you're on plates, thanks. I'll serve it up, so pass them over one at a time. Cheese crust for whoever wants the corner, and I suspect I know who that is.
lines.do: Carries the pie to the table, sets it on a mat and picks up the serving spoon.

lines.name: Jack Whitfield
lines.say: Go on then, plates, I'm on it. Honestly, dad, that corner is mine, you know me too well. Mum, you want a big bit or a small bit? Careful, Soph, it's boiling.
lines.do: Gets up, takes the warm plates from the side using the oven gloves and passes them to Andrew one at a time

lines.name: Julie Whitfield
lines.say: Small bit for me, love, I'm not that hungry, bless you. Ooh, that smells lovely, Andrew. Jack, mind your sleeve on the gravy! Sophie, pass the sauce to your dad, would you? Right, everyone got a drink? Shall I pour the water?
lines.do: Holds her plate out to Andrew and reaches for the water jug

lines.name: Sophie Whitfield
lines.say: Yeah, I'll have water, thanks mum. Dad, just a normal bit for me, not a huge one. And Jack, you can have the corner, I'm not fighting you for it.
lines.do: Passes the sauce across to Andrew and holds out her plate.

lines.name: Andrew Whitfield
lines.say: Here you go, Julie, small bit, with plenty of cheese on top. Jack, corner's yours, and mind the plate, it's hot. Soph, a normal bit, coming up. Right, sauce, thanks. Everyone dig in before it goes cold.
lines.do: Serves the pie onto each plate in turn, passing them round, then sits down with his own.

lines.name: Jack Whitfield
lines.say: Mate, that corner is perfect, honestly. Cheers, dad. Mum, do you want the sauce or are you good? Soph, did you see the state of me with that oven glove, I nearly dropped the lot. Right, what are we watching after this, is it the reality stuff or the footy?
lines.do: Sits down with plate, digs into the cheesy corner
